chunks: What Saʿd narrated from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Rāzī, who said:

I was with some companions of mine on a journey, and I was their Imam. I performed the maghrib salat, then gave salām after the first two rakʿahs. My companions said, “You only performed two rakʿahs for us.” I spoke to them and they spoke to me, and they said, “As for us, we will repeat.” I said, “But I will not repeat; rather, I will complete it with one rakʿah.” So I completed it with one rakʿah. Then we departed, and I came to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and mentioned to him what had occurred in our matter. He said to me, “You were more correct than they in action. Only the one who does not know how much he has prayed repeats.”

Thus, he عليه السلام clarified in this report that whoever does not know what he has prayed must repeat, as opposed to one who is certain. Alongside that, in the two hadiths there is that which prevents reliance upon them, namely the hadith of Dhū al-Shimālayn and the forgetfulness of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and that is among the things prevented by decisive proofs establishing that forgetfulness and error are not permissible for him صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.

key_terms.إِمَامُهُمْ: their Imam; the one leading the congregational salat
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the first two rakʿahs after which salām was mistakenly given
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: journey; the setting in which the incident took place
key_terms.الْإِعَادَةُ: repeating the prayer from the beginning
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the maghrib salat, which consists of three rakʿahs
key_terms.تَيَقَّنَ: became certain; having certainty about what was performed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone gives salām after two rakʿahs in maghrib salat and then realizes the mistake?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on forgetting in maghrib salat: if a person is certain that one rakʿah remains, he completes the prayer rather than repeating it. It also states that repetition is required only for one who does not know how much he has prayed, while affirming the Shia principle that forgetfulness and error are not permissible for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
